questions.title: The RLVR boundary
questions.prompt: Choose the only case that is **by itself** RLVR training.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. RLVR uses a verifiable outcome inside the policy-learning update. A is test-time search, C is supervised learning on filtered data, and D is reranking without parameter updates.

options.text: The model samples 32 solutions, tests select the best, and weights stay fixed.
Deterministic test outcomes are used as rewards in a policy update.
The model is supervised-fine-tuned on solutions that happened to pass tests.
A reward model reranks responses only for display.

questions.title: Probability of an informative group
questions.prompt: A binary reward has single-sample success probability $p=0.25$ and group size $G=4$. Compute the probability that the group contains at least one success and at least one failure.
questions.explanation:
$$
P_{\mathrm{info}}=1-p^G-(1-p)^G
=1-0.25^4-0.75^4=0.6796875.
$$

The calculation assumes conditionally independent samples. Correlated completions provide less effective diversity.

questions.title: The denominator policy
questions.prompt: Completions were generated by policy revision `v17`; optimization is now evaluating `v19`; KL is measured to a frozen SFT model. Which policy belongs in the probability-ratio denominator?
questions.explanation: The denominator is the **actual behavior policy `v17`**, including the decoding transformations used during sampling. `v19` is the current policy and the SFT model is the reference anchor; neither can replace the source of the stored actions.

questions.title: Advantages in a symmetric group
questions.prompt: A group has rewards $[1,1,0,0]$. Compute the advantages after subtracting the mean and dividing by the population standard deviation.
questions.explanation:
The mean is $0.5$ and the population standard deviation is also $0.5$, hence

$$
\widehat A=[1,1,-1,-1].
$$

They sum to zero. These are response-level signals, not causal token-level credit assignments.

questions.title: When clipping is active
questions.prompt: For ratio $\rho=1.35$, advantage $A=2$, and symmetric clip interval $[0.8,1.2]$, compute the unclipped and clipped terms. Which branch enters the minimum?
questions.explanation: The unclipped term is $1.35\cdot2=2.70$. The clipped term is $1.2\cdot2=2.40$, so the minimum is $2.40$. With positive advantage, upper clipping limits further incentive to increase an already enlarged ratio.

questions.title: Implicit prompt reweighting
questions.prompt: Two groups have centered rewards $[-0.1,0.1]$ and $[-1,1]$. What happens after each group is divided by its own standard deviation? Why is this not neutral?
questions.explanation: Both become $[-1,1]$. Per-group standardization removes the difference in raw reward scale and therefore reweights prompts: a small, possibly noisy gap receives the same normalized magnitude as a large gap. This may stabilize numbers, but it changes the objective’s weighting.

questions.title: Length and reduction unit
questions.prompt: Two responses have equal-magnitude advantages and lengths 20 and 200. Compare per-response token averaging with one global average over all active tokens.
questions.explanation: Per-response averaging gives equal total weight to the responses, so each short-response token has ten times the coefficient. A global active-token average gives equal token coefficients, so the long response receives about ten times the total contribution. The reduction unit is part of the objective, not a cosmetic implementation choice.

questions.title: The four DAPO components
questions.prompt: Name the four changes bundled in DAPO and explain why “we use DAPO” is insufficient for reproducibility.
questions.explanation: DAPO highlights **Clip-Higher**, **Dynamic Sampling**, **Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss** with global token normalization, and **Overlong Reward Shaping**. A reproducible run still needs group and batch sizes, clip bounds, degenerate-group handling, exact reduction, KL choices, truncation and length rules, and policy revisions. Implementations may use only part of the recipe or combine it with other variants.

questions.title: GSPO sequence ratio
questions.prompt: The token ratios are $(1.21,0.81)$. Compute the length-normalized GSPO sequence ratio.
questions.explanation:
$$
s=\exp\left(\frac{\log1.21+\log0.81}{2}\right)
=\sqrt{1.21\cdot0.81}=0.99.
$$

This is the geometric mean of token ratios. It is GSPO’s normalized sequence construction, not the exact full-sequence likelihood-ratio product.

questions.title: Entropy is not diversity
questions.prompt: A model produces 64 nearly identical strings with punctuation variation. Mean token entropy remains high, but every answer uses the same wrong algorithm. What should be measured in addition to token entropy?
questions.explanation: Measure outcome and response-level diversity: pass@k or success@k, unique normalized answers, semantic or strategy clusters, length distribution, and repeated-template rates. Local uncertainty can be spent on surface form without creating new solution strategies.

questions.title: Terminal or truncation
questions.prompt: A response hits `max_new_tokens` without EOS. Why should it not automatically be treated as an ordinary incorrect terminal? Give two defensible treatments and their risks.
questions.explanation: The limit is an external truncation: the eventual outcome is unobserved. Excluding the response reduces ambiguous noise but may let the policy evade negative reward by continuing forever. A declared soft length penalty encourages completion but can shorten genuinely difficult reasoning prematurely. The stop reason must be logged separately in either case.

questions.title: Reading the teaching run
questions.prompt: In the teaching run, mean training-prompt accuracy rises from 0.31 to 0.41, entropy roughly halves, and held-out success disappears. Which conclusion is justified?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. The small reproducible run demonstrates a possible concentration and train–transfer gap. It does not establish a universal property of GRPO, a universal entropy threshold, or a verifier bug.

options.text: Optimization improved measured reward on part of the training distribution, while coverage and transfer required separate diagnosis.
